title: DerivativeRegister
description:
POST /derivatives/register — the on-device AI contribute-back (OL-1). A consumer that computed expensive, identity-bearing AI on-device (Apple FeaturePrint/Vision embeddings, faces, OCR, Speech transcripts, auto-tags, aesthetics — the LoupeJSON `ai` block) FIRST writes the blob through the mount to <nas_root>/.juicemount/derivatives/<inode>/ai.loupe.json (it has write access), THEN calls this to make the server index it so every other client + the web UI reuses it. SUPERSEDED by REGISTER-ROUTE (2026-08-04): this route is no longer AI-only. A consumer may commit `ai`, `proxy`, `thumbnail` and `waveform` blobs it generated on-device. `tech` remains server-only (it is ffprobe output, not an artifact), and `filmstrip` is withheld until its reader contract is specified. Requires the `contribute-derivatives` capability token. The server is the source-hash authority: the consumer cannot compute the contract xxh3 (it uses xxh64), so it VOUCHES with source_size+source_mtime (the live stat it computed the AI against); the server re-stats and accepts ONLY on a size+mtime match (else 409 — the AI was computed against stale bytes), then stamps the canonical xxh3 itself.

REQUEST body (application/json): { inode:int, kind:"ai"|"proxy"|"thumbnail"|"waveform", producer:"on-device"|"macos-node", model:string, dim:int, source_size:int, source_mtime:int, blob_rel_path:string }. REGISTER-ROUTE (2026-08-04): blob_rel_path MUST equal the reserved filename for the kind (WRITE_PLACEMENT §2) or the request is rejected 400 — the consumer does not choose a path inside the provider namespace; for kind==ai it may be omitted and is resolved to whichever of ai.logger.json / ai.loupe.json is on disk. The blob MUST already exist: the server stats it and returns 409 if absent, so a row is never minted for a blob that is not there (WRITE_PLACEMENT §4 — the row is the commit point). The size/mtime vouch and the server-side re-stat apply to every kind, not just ai.

This document is the 200 RESPONSE.

inode.description: Echo of the registered asset's JuiceFS inode.

registered.description: true on a successful register (200). A conflicting register returns HTTP 409 with a discriminated body — see register-conflict.schema.json (VERSION 3).

derivative.description: The manifest row the server wrote — identical shape to a derivatives.schema.json entry. The server stamped source_hash (its own xxh3), updated_at, and status:ready.

kind.description: WIDENED AGAIN 2026-08-05: filmstrip and audio_proxy are now registrable, so EVERY blob-bearing kind can be contributed. filmstrip was previously withheld because its reader contract was unspecified; that contract is now written down AND ENFORCED at register (see `filmstrip`), so a strip that reaches the index is renderable by any client by definition. `tech` remains server-only (it is ffprobe output, not an artifact) and `ai` left the derivative store entirely by founder ruling 2026-08-04 — the document belongs in the clip sidecar, which has a real per-field CRDT, not in a namespace whose contract is 'rebuildable, safe to purge'.

producer.description: Who computed it. on-device = Apple frameworks / BYO cloud key on a Mac.

hash.description: The server's canonical xxh3 of the source (== source_hash). On-device consumers verify with size/mtime, not this; an xxh3-capable client/web UI can verify by hash.

blob_rel_path.description: Volume-relative under /.juicemount/derivatives/<inode>/. Reserved per kind and NOT chooseable by the contributor — a mismatch is 400.

media_type.description: ASSIGNED BY THE SERVER FROM `kind`, never echoed from the request: /blob pins its response Content-Type from this field, so a contributor-supplied value would be a contributor-controlled Content-Type served from the control-plane origin. ai/waveform => application/json, proxy => video/mp4, audio_proxy => audio/mp4, thumbnail/filmstrip => image/jpeg.

model.description: Embedding model id+version so kNN partitions by space (e.g. apple-featureprint-v1 vs the portable openclip-vit-b32-v1).

source_size.description: The server's authoritative (re-stat'd) source size in bytes — echoes the vouched value on accept, so any client's read-gate can stat-verify off the manifest.

source_mtime.description: The server's authoritative (re-stat'd) source mtime (unix seconds).

codec.description: REQUIRED on the REQUEST for kind proxy/audio_proxy, and DECLARATIVE rather than gated (founder decision 2026-08-04, superseding the H.264 floor). A node contributes what it CAN do; the fleet's output is the union, not the intersection, and a codec floor lets the least capable node set the ceiling for every node. Any value in this enum is accepted; a value OUTSIDE it is refused, because a codec a reader cannot RECOGNISE is worse than one it cannot decode — it cannot even choose. Still required because an ABSENT codec is defined as h264, so silence mislabels a richer codec rather than describing it.

codec_string.description: Exact MediaSource.isTypeSupported / canPlayType token, e.g. avc1.640028 or hvc1.1.6.L93.B0. Echoed from the request; the reader checks the row before fetching.

width.description: ARTIFACT DESCRIPTOR (2026-08-04). Pixel width for thumbnail/proxy/audio_proxy/filmstrip. Lets a server rank a contributed artifact WITHOUT decoding it, so a cheap one can be earmarked for upgrade by a more capable node or the farm. Distinct from `dim`, which is embedding dimensionality. Rejected 400 on a kind where pixels are not meaningful.

bitrate_bps.description: ARTIFACT DESCRIPTOR. Encoded bitrate for proxy/audio_proxy only. Together with width/height it makes an upgrade policy a comparison rather than a decode — blob_size alone is a bad quality proxy, since a flat LOG-graded 720 frame can encode smaller than a busy 320.

filmstrip.description: REQUIRED for kind==filmstrip, rejected 400 on any other kind. THE READER CONTRACT, enforced at register: LAYOUT row-major, origin TOP-LEFT, ZERO gutter — cell (r,c) occupies x=[c*cell_w,(c+1)*cell_w), y=[r*cell_h,(r+1)*cell_h). CANVAS exactly cols*cell_w by rows*cell_h, no padding or border, so a cell rect is pure multiplication. ORIENTATION frames are stored UPRIGHT AS DISPLAYED; source rotation is already applied and a reader must NOT re-apply it. FRAME i is at row i/cols, col i%cols, for i in [0,frame_count). TRAILING cols*rows MAY exceed frame_count; cells at index >= frame_count are UNDEFINED and must not be rendered — ignoring this is what silently yields a duplicated or black last frame. TIME frame i covers [i*interval_ms,(i+1)*interval_ms) of a duration_ms source. Bounds: cols/rows 1..4096, cell_w/cell_h 1..8192, interval_ms >= 1, frame_count <= cols*rows.
